title: Wild Rice Salad with Cranberry and Pecan
subtitle: Nutty wild rice with dried cranberries, toasted pecans and orange dressing
excerpt: Wild rice mixed with dried cranberries, toasted pecans, celery and spring onion, dressed in orange juice and cider vinegar. A salad for autumn and winter that works alongside roast poultry or as a stand-alone grain salad.
sourceNotes: Wild rice salad with cranberries and nuts is a Thanksgiving and autumn staple of North American cooking, reflecting the native American origins of wild rice (Zizania species) and cranberries. The salad came to British cooking via American food writing and the spread of wild rice and dried cranberries in UK supermarkets from the late 1990s.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Keeps well for a buffet.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the wild rice and dress while warm; it can sit at room temperature for several hours.

content.text: Wild rice salad with cranberry and pecan earns its place on the autumn table for its colour and texture as much as its flavour: the dark grain, the red dried fruit, the golden nuts. It holds well for hours, travels, and is one of the few salads that actually improves sitting under clingfilm for a few hours. The orange dressing brings acidity and lift.

Put {{wild-rice}} of wild rice in a saucepan with 600 ml of cold water and a generous pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 40 to 45 minutes until the grains are tender and many have begun to split open. Drain any excess water. The rice should be chewy, not hard.

While the rice is still warm, whisk together the {{orange-juice}} of orange juice, {{cider-vinegar}} of cider vinegar, {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Pour over the warm rice and toss to coat.

Leave the rice to cool for 10 minutes, then stir in the {{dried-cranberries}} of dried cranberries, {{pecans}} of toasted pecans, the celery and spring onion. Scatter over the parsley if using. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve at room temperature.

items.symptom: Rice is still hard after 45 minutes
items.cause: Wild rice is tough and takes longer than other grains.
items.fix: Continue cooking for another 10 minutes with the lid on. Wild rice can take up to 55 minutes depending on the variety. Look for grains that have split to reveal the white interior.

items.cause: Wild rice absorbs the dressing as it sits.
items.fix: Dress generously while the rice is warm. Reserve a small amount of the dressing to stir through before serving.

content.text: Wild rice comes from the Great Lakes region and has been harvested by Native American communities for thousands of years. It became a mainstream American ingredient in the 20th century, and the autumn salad with cranberry and pecan is now a Thanksgiving staple. It arrived in British cooking in the late 1990s as dried cranberries and wild rice reached supermarkets. It sits well alongside roast turkey, duck or pheasant.
